acceptanceCriteria.description: Every container with an exact declared slot exposes an accessible Add element action; the modal shows only compatible bounded candidates, handles multiple destination regions, supports unassigned visual reuse, and immediately selects, focuses, and reveals the inserted child.

Users can add, move, and deterministically reorder eligible assets without pointer or keyboard drag behavior, while canonical ordered AssetPlacement records, compatibility, bounds, undo, save, validation, and recursive preview remain authoritative.

The Asset Palette is removed and layouts appear in a collapsible bar directly below Design and Connections, with layout data requested only after the bar is opened and existing reviewed layout-change semantics preserved.

The eager Composer catalog omits configuration schemas and defaults; selecting an asset requests only its exact workspace-scoped property detail, stale responses cannot replace newer selections, and leaving Properties or Styling releases inactive detail rather than growing an unbounded cache.

Desktop and thin client expose identical summary, detail, modal composition, loading, empty, error, keyboard, focus-restoration, and failure behavior through their real IPC and HTTP client boundaries.

Focused instrumentation proves no Canvas node registers drag/drop/sort behavior, modal compatibility and layout reads are demand-driven and bounded, selection changes do not reload the full catalog, and representative nested reference systems preserve complete Canvas and preview hierarchy without new render or request loops.

Applicable typechecks, desktop and thin-client builds, documentation, architecture, agent-support, packaging, and full test gates pass once after the complete increment, with any environment-limited qualification reported explicitly.

steps: Add and verify lightweight catalog summaries and exact workspace-scoped definition detail across application, API, IPC/preload, desktop, and thin-client boundaries.
Build and verify the shared asset-selection modal, destination-region selection, add/reuse/focus flow, explicit move/order actions, and collapsible on-demand layout bar.

plan.summary: Deliver one cohesive vertical increment: establish a lightweight summary/exact-detail boundary, replace palette dragging with an accessible container-scoped modal plus explicit movement controls and a lazy layout bar, then qualify the complete shared experience and measured loading behavior.

risks: Removing schemas/defaults from summaries can break add and inspector behavior unless exact detail is loaded before creating a new instance and when selection changes.
Containers with multiple slots need an explicit destination choice or the modal could create invalid placements.
Removing drag without replacement controls would regress move and order behavior.
Styling edits depend on the root definition even when another instance is selected and therefore need an explicit active-tab detail exception.
Full nested Canvas rendering can still be expensive after drag removal; structural projections and node props must remain stable and measured rather than indiscriminately memoized.

Foundation definitions can be projected outside an older exact Asset Library activation, so the exact-detail operation must retain the existing trusted Composer-only fallback without widening general Asset Library visibility.
research.summary: The existing ordered draft commands already add, attach, reparent, and remove instances independently of dnd-kit, so the canonical mutation layer can remain. The eager list use case expands every card into a full definition; splitting the read model into structural summaries and one exact detail operation is the smallest truthful lazy boundary. The shared ModalDialog and TabbedPanel provide the required accessibility foundations, while the current editor and workspace tests cover nested hierarchy, layouts, properties, preview, and transport parity.

increments.rollback: Restore the previous shared Composer surface and eager catalog client while preserving all existing immutable revisions, placements, definitions, configurations, and layout selections. The additive exact-detail read can remain unused safely; rollback must not flatten or rewrite canonical hierarchy.

Run focused request-count, stale-response, retained-detail, nested hierarchy, recursive preview, and representative reference-system regression tests.

After all internal work packages pass, run the applicable desktop/thin-client builds and npm run docs:check, npm run architecture:check, npm run agent-support:check, npm run package, and npm test once as increment completion gates.
